author: Gian López
abstract: Standards for the part of a web UI that is the same regardless of the meta-framework rendering it: the markup that carries the meaning and the TailwindCSS v4 theme that presents it. Semantic elements first, because the element is what makes a page machine-readable and its structure legible; then TailwindCSS v4, where styling resolves through theme tokens rather than arbitrary values, sized to the project — one plain theme by default, the variable-backed semantic layer only where a component generator or a theme swap reads it; then the two defects utility CSS makes easiest to ship, layout shift and a stylesheet that never saw half its classes. Framework-specific concerns — forms libraries, component generators, compiler behavior — live in react-best-practices and astro-best-practices, which load this skill alongside their own. Accessibility auditing is excluded by design
